title: BridgePermissionMessages
description: WebSocket envelopes — bridge permission RPC (Strategy B PreToolUse hook). Outbound permission_request (bridge → backend) plus the matching command.claude.permission.allow|deny decision RPC (backend → bridge). Cross-reference: docs/design/v1-permission-blockers.md §2.1.3 (envelope schema) and §2.2.2 (decision RPC).

messages.description: Bridge surfaces a pending tool call to backend so the user can approve/deny before the claude CLI executes the tool. Fired from inside the bridge's PreToolUse hook path (Strategy B per design doc §2.1.1). Backend translates this envelope into the existing iOS-bound `question` MessageType (see approval-messages.json). The envelope's outer correlation_id always carries the originating command.claude.run rpc_id so the backend orchestrator can route the event into the correct per-session subscriber queue.

session_id.description: Lead claude session UUID. For sub-agent originated requests this is still the lead session id (the sub-agent task id lives in parent_task_id) so backend can attribute the question to the correct iOS connection.

request_id.description: Bridge-generated UUIDv7 (time-ordered). Serves as the decision-correlation token: iOS echoes it back via approval_response and the backend re-broadcasts it on the inbound command.claude.permission.allow|deny RPC. The bridge's permission Broker keys its in-flight UDS waiters by this id.

tool_name.description: Canonical (post-aliased) claude tool name — e.g. `Bash`, `Edit`, `Write`, `WebFetch`. Matches the keys in the bridge-side risk classification table.

tool_input.description: Verbatim claude PreToolUse payload. Preserved as a raw JSON object so the backend can decode it into Pydantic without an intermediate Go schema bound. May carry sensitive content (Bash commands with secrets, file paths with PII); backend MUST NOT log this field at info level — see runbook §11 + design §4.5.

input_preview.description: Truncated text representation of tool_input suitable for iOS display without leaking large file diffs or full Bash command lines. Bridge-side truncation, capped at 240 bytes.

risk.description: Bridge-classified risk band. Classification authority lives in the bridge — it has direct access to cwd, can compare paths, and knows the bash whitelist. Backend translates this to ApprovalCategory (high → DESTRUCTIVE, medium → WRITE_REMOTE, low → INFRASTRUCTURE) via the runbook §4 table.

reason.description: Optional free-form audit string explaining why approval was needed (e.g. 'whitelist miss', 'off-cwd write', 'unknown plugin tool'). Surfaced into structured logs and the audit_log row.

timeout_ms.description: Bridge-suggested decision ceiling (default 30000ms). Backend forwards this as `timeout_seconds` in the iOS QUESTION payload (clamping the per-category default — see V1.4-fix HIGH commit 811ea0f). Bridge's UDS broker timeout = timeout_ms + 4s grace; claude CLI hook timeout left at 60s default (well above this ceiling per design §2.2.4).

parent_task_id.description: Set when the PreToolUse hook fires from inside a sub-agent task. Backend uses this to attribute the question to the lead session_id rather than the sub-agent task_id.

messages.description: Backend dispatches an `allow` decision back to the originating bridge. Bridge `dispatchCommand` looks up the permission Broker singleton and calls `broker.Resolve(request_id, Allow)` — the matching in-flight UDS hook connection unblocks, prints `{"decision": "allow"}` to stdout, and the claude CLI proceeds with the tool call. Sent by `_await_and_dispatch_decision` after `approval_service.wait_for_decision(...)` resolves to approved. The envelope's outer correlation_id echoes the originating command.claude.run rpc_id (though the broker itself routes by request_id, not by correlation_id).

session_id.description: Lead claude session UUID. Echoes the value from the originating event.session.permission_request for observability + audit (the broker's UDS hook routes purely by request_id).

request_id.description: UUID from the originating event.session.permission_request envelope. The bridge's permission Broker keys its in-flight UDS waiters by this value; mismatch = noop.

decision.description: Hard-coded to `allow` for this envelope type. The matching deny envelope uses type=command.claude.permission.deny with decision=`deny`.

reason.description: Optional free-form audit string surfaced into structured logs. For user-driven approvals this is typically blank (the audit row already captures the user_id + responded_at).

updated_input.description: Reserved for the MCP-style `permission_prompt_tool returns a modified tool_input` branch. **Ignored by V1** — the broker forwards the original tool_input unchanged. Future V2/V3 work may wire this through the broker into the hook reply.

messages.description: Backend dispatches a `deny` decision back to the originating bridge. Bridge `dispatchCommand` looks up the permission Broker singleton and calls `broker.Resolve(request_id, Deny)` — the matching in-flight UDS hook connection unblocks, prints `{"decision": "block", "reason": "user denied"}` to stdout, and the claude CLI cancels the tool call. Sent by `_await_and_dispatch_decision` for three sources: explicit user reject, RFApprovalSheet auto-timeout, or `bridge_registry.send_to_bridge` failure (bridge offline → automatic deny per the deny-on-timeout invariant in runbook §7).

session_id.description: Lead claude session UUID. Echoes the value from the originating event.session.permission_request for observability + audit (the broker's UDS hook routes purely by request_id).

request_id.description: UUID from the originating event.session.permission_request envelope. The bridge's permission Broker keys its in-flight UDS waiters by this value; mismatch = noop.

decision.description: Hard-coded to `deny` for this envelope type. The matching allow envelope uses type=command.claude.permission.allow with decision=`allow`.

reason.description: Optional free-form audit string surfaced into structured logs. Backend populates this with the timeout source (`user denied`, `timeout`, `dispatch_failed`) so the bridge-side audit + the hook stdout reason field stay in sync.

updated_input.description: Reserved for symmetry with the allow envelope — never set on a deny path. Ignored by V1.
